title: The $(4/3,2)$-hypercontractive inequality at $\rho=1/\sqrt3$
statement:
For every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, applying the noise operator with
parameter $\rho=1/\sqrt3$ contracts the $L^2$ norm below the $L^{4/3}$ norm of the
original function:
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[(T_{1/\sqrt3} f)^2\bigr]\bigr)^{1/2}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{4/3}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{3/4},
\]
where both expectations are taken under the uniform measure on the hypercube. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
hypotheses_covered: f is an arbitrary Boolean function of arity n (f : {0,1}^n → ℝ)
replaced:
Boolean functions are $(4/3, 2)$-hypercontractive with parameter $1/\sqrt3$: for any
$f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$,
\[
  \bigl(\E[(T_{1/\sqrt3} f)^2]\bigr)^{1/2}
  \le \bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^{4/3}\,]\bigr)^{3/4}.
\]
